assumptions.statement: All labor for water maintenance must be tracked in commons hours to avoid hidden labor burden and ensure maintenance_hours limits.
Resident capacity is limited by available_commons_hours and hours_per_resident metrics observed in baseline simulations.

expected_effects.rationale: Explicit tracking ensures burden is not shifted or hidden.
Maintains labor visibility without creating new demand.

hypothesis: Labor for water reserve maintenance must be explicitly tracked to avoid hidden labor burdens and ensure maintenance_hours remain within available_commons_hours.

queries: water labor telemetry baseline simulation hours per resident maintenance events storage recovery hours

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Automated logging where possible; manual audit required only if automation unavailable.
Prioritize critical load reserves and safety checks in rotation.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Maintenance delays may affect water safety

acceptance_tests: No labor is shifted into untracked resident burden.
Privacy, consent, public-health, accessibility, and governance assumptions remain explicit.

title: Water Maintenance Labor Tracking Protocol
